matrix.example: Amada Bata: reading becomes stage sound
matrix.section: Writing between stage, radio and cinema
matrix.evidence_type: Original printed stage directions; complete first scene inspected in retained dossier
matrix.contribution: Maya’s reading can be represented by instrumental music and offstage character voices.

matrix.section: What a story asks us to notice
matrix.evidence_type: Original novel reading, separately verified original film credit cards
matrix.contribution: A concrete first-person doorway encounter gives the reader a literary experience; film credits establish credited source author.
matrix.boundary: The 1977 printing is not established as first publication. Credits do not prove fidelity or equivalent staging. Silent film samples do not resolve point of view.
matrix.recommendation: Retain opening encounter. Completed novel reading supports it without requiring plot expansion. Link to the music chapter’s poem subsection if useful.

matrix.section: What a story asks us to notice
matrix.evidence_type: Identified original-text transcriptions and bounded English renderings
matrix.contribution: Listening, pictures and the narrator’s irony make reading itself an experience rather than a bibliography.
matrix.boundary: No demonstrated filmed equivalents; textual interpretation is not historical audience response.
matrix.recommendation: Retain bounded observations and source/translation attribution; no new adaptation claim.

matrix.evidence_type: Complete short-story transcription plus separately attributed actor interview
matrix.contribution: Villagers’ complaints coexist with their reliance on Ananta’s work; the actor states an intention for the later performance.
matrix.boundary: Actor intention is not reception or fidelity. Transcription is not a verified historical edition; fiction is not livelihood statistics.
matrix.recommendation: Retain separation of story detail from performance intention.

matrix.evidence_type: Director’s published first-person book-handover account plus official trailer-description credits
matrix.contribution: A producer team brings a book to a director; credits distinguish original story/dialogue from shared screenplay.
matrix.boundary: Novel text/imprint remains uninspected; no reading of Nadabindu, rights terms or fidelity inferred. Trailer metadata is not original film-credit inspection.
matrix.recommendation: Retain this strongest concrete collaboration example rather than adding a generic synopsis.

matrix.evidence_type: Official IFFI press account; Film Bazaar writer credit retained in dedicated chapter
matrix.contribution: Concise contemporary source-story connection, with a route to the film and maker chapters.
matrix.boundary: PIB names inspiration but not story title or adaptation decisions. Its remake token concerns film rights, not original-author remuneration; announcement is not a completed remake.
matrix.recommendation: Retain. Family encouragement is already in Anupam’s profile; Roshan Bisoi’s writing is already in Pratikshya. Repeating either does not close the source-story gap.

matrix.section: The connection continues; When a film brings a book into view

supported_claims.claim: The interview question identifies Gourahari Das’s source short story as Bapa; Patnaik responds that he connected with the story when reading it.
supported_claims.evidence_type: Interviewer’s identification plus director response; not inspection of the original story edition.

supported_claims.claim: Patnaik explains Pratikshya as a title broad enough for waiting for work, marriage and settling down, rather than only the father relationship.
supported_claims.evidence_type: Published first-person account of title choice.

fresh_lead.proposed_paraphrase: Anupam Patnaik explained why Gourahari Das’s Bapa became Pratikshya: the film concerned more than a father. Waiting for a job, marriage and a settled life gave him the broader title. The choice names a filmmaker’s reading of his source.
fresh_lead.proposed_destination: Dedicated Pratikshya chapter, beside the source-story connection; prefer a compact replacement/enrichment over repeating in Anupam and literature. Coordinator should determine adoption after independent source review.
fresh_lead.proposed_note: Ashok Palit, interview with Anupam Patnaik, The Pioneer, 14 December 2022, p2.
limits: No original Bapa text, edition or author permission inspected.
Title-choice testimony does not independently demonstrate additions to or departures from the original story.
Do not infer payment, remake completion or reception.
Do not adopt unrelated headline opinions or internally inconsistent award-year references.
January2023 Odisha News Times reprint is a related source, not independent corroboration; parent reports404.
